notes.sol: The pinned original revision 1 and SCORE repaired revision 3 are distinct targets. Revision 1 has a pre-output blocker; all affected claims C1-C8 are not_checkable P0, independently of the extra unseeded parallel-bootstrap ambiguity on C1-C5. SCORE C6 2.9574 and C7/C8 matching values come from the repaired workflow and are retained as diagnostics. C6 discrepant is not accepted without evidence that the same intended inputs and procedure produce it. Technical failure is primary; computational issues is the partial-run alternative. No number from the repaired version is used as a scoring reference.
notes.claude: Technical failure, alternative computational issues. All eight claims are not_checkable P0 because the pipeline stops before any output; SCORE's values come from a repaired run on a substituted intermediate and are non-scoring diagnostics. Reconciled with the second labeller (see reconciliation.md). The final judgement is the structured label; notes_blind_original keeps the pre-reconciliation blind notes, which are historical and superseded wherever they conflict with the final label.
notes.claude_blind_original_historical: SCORE push-button attempt: 'Completed claim(s): none'. The shipped script (SHA matches the pin) uses interactive file.choose(), calls functions since renamed in SemNetCleaner/SemNeT (partboot, partboot.test), and calls autoDeStr(binary, ...) where the object is 'bin'. The analyst skipped the first 30 lines, loaded Cleaning File.Rdata, renamed functions and copied old helpers from GitHub. No set.seed anywhere, and partboot uses cores=4. The analyst also notes 'even with setting a seed the outcome can be different each time'. Some Table 3 cells fall outside SCORE's approximate band despite the analyst's boilerplate line (CC 70%: 27.995 vs 36.38; ASPL 50%: -16.306 vs -12.27; ASPL 60%: -23.439 vs -20.01; CC 50%: 17.927 vs 21.71). The likely causes are package versions and the unseeded bootstrap. C6 is the main judgement call (see rationale). The claim list has no problems, and its reported values match the manuscript.
